implementation_notes: encoding/json turns struct tags into the mapping metadata: json.Marshal walks the graph and returns a []byte that the driver binds straight to a BLOB/TEXT/JSONB column, and json.Unmarshal rebuilds it, so the serializer class of the classic pattern disappears. Unexported fields are skipped, cycles fail at runtime and interface values need registered concrete types, which makes the payload a projection of the struct rather than a complete copy.
pitfalls: json.Marshal skips unexported fields and rejects function, channel and cyclic values, so the stored graph can quietly lose state.
time.Time and large int64 values change shape on the wire (RFC 3339 text, float64 precision for some consumers); use json.Number or a custom type when that matters.
Scanning a NULL column into []byte fails, so nullable graphs need a pointer, sql.Null[[]byte] or a COALESCE in the query.

variants.name: encoding/gob binary blob
variants.implementation_notes: encoding/gob encodes Go values into a compact binary stream with no tags: one Encoder writes the whole graph into a buffer that goes to a BYTEA/BLOB column and one Decoder reads it back. It is Go-specific and stream-oriented, so it suits internal caches and checkpoints where size matters and no other language will read the payload; interface-typed fields require gob.Register of every concrete type.
pitfalls: Interface-typed fields fail to encode unless each concrete type is registered with gob.Register, and renamed or moved types break decoding of stored blobs.
The gob stream is not self-delimiting for storage: keep exactly one Encode call's bytes per row or the decoder will consume the next value.
